messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up on paged/blocked KV + attention kernel compatibility. After the RFC we still don't have a concrete plan for: eviction+fragmentation interaction, presenting a contiguous KV view to kernels, and safe/cheap fallbacks. Putting up a few concrete options and tradeoffs.

maria: +1 we hit this in prod sims. TL;DR problems I saw: heavy fragmentation causes lots of small GPU gathers, kernel microkernels expect long contiguous KV segments for vectorized gather/scatter.

sanjay: Can you list the options? I want to run cost math (copy vs scatter throughput).

alex: Options I had in mind: 1) Stitch-on-copy: CPU/host-side coalesce fragments into a contiguous buffer, then memcpy to GPU. Pros: keeps existing kernels. Cons: extra mem & copy, P95 latency hit for some requests. 2) Scatter-gather kernel: implement kernel-level indirect gathers from multiple blocks (no host copy). Pros: avoids copy; cons: kernel complexity, lots of small reads, may lose vectorization. 3) Hot-pinning: keep hot KV entries in a contiguous "hot pool" so typical short-window workloads rarely touch fragments. Pros: low-latency for common case; cons: requires promotion heuristics + memory overhead. 4) Incremental compaction: background compaction that merges fragments into larger blocks during low load. Pros: long-term fragmentation reduction; cons: adds GC/lock complexity + pointer churn.

megan: Also we need a clean API surface between pager and kernel. I propose a small interface: `PageView` that returns either `ContiguousHandle` (GPU ptr) or `ScatterList` (list of <block,offset,len>) and a flag `requires_copy`. Kernels try to accept Contiguous first, otherwise request a copy from pager.

maria: That sounds good. We should be explicit about pin counts + eviction listeners. If a kernel asks for a `ContiguousHandle` the pager must pin involved pages until `release_handle()` is called, otherwise we race with eviction.

sanjay: Important perf numbers to collect before choosing: copy bandwidth p50/p95, scatter gather throughput measured with our attention gather pattern, and fraction of requests that are >1 fragment. Add metrics: `kv.fragmentation_ratio`, `kv.stitch_copy_rate`, `kernel.scatter_throughput`.

alex: Agreed. Also tradeoff: for very long sequences we can split attention into smaller windows handled by kernel with local KV view; that's a fallback that avoids huge contiguous allocations. But splitting changes attention semantics for some algorithms (relative pos enc, rotary offsets), so we need to verify correctness.

megan: On the compaction side, incremental compaction needs to be crash-safe. We should rely on a two-phase commit pattern: allocate new block, copy live entries, update index atomically, then free old block. Keep compaction unit small (e.g., 4-8MB) to bound work.

maria: For eviction policy, LRU isn't enough when attention locality vs token frequency differ. Suggest hybrid: recency weighted by access span (how many different sequences touch the entry). That helps not evict long-lived KV used across many sequences.

sanjay: On implementation: scatter-list passing could be zero-copy if kernel supports GPU-side gather from a list of device pointers. That requires us to store block pages already in device memory (nicer for Dedicated deployments), or issue peer DMA. For hosted inference we might prefer host-copy approach. So runtime should pick per-deployment strategy.

alex: Good point. Let's expose `pager.capabilities` at startup: {device_pages: bool, max_scatter_entries: n, zero_copy: bool}. Kernels query runtime and pick execution path.

megan: Tests: microbench for 1) single-request multi-fragment gather cost 2) stitch latency p95 with different fragment counts 3) compaction impact on throughput during background passes 4) correctness tests for split-window attention with rotary/relative positions.

alex: Backward-compat: if pager returns `unsupported` for scatter and providing contiguous is too expensive, kernel should fall back to older non-paged kernel that keeps full KV per-request (i.e., memory blowup but correctness maintained). This is last resort.

maria: Ops notes: we should surface an alert when `kv.fragmentation_ratio > 0.6` AND `kv.stitch_copy_rate > 100/s` — indicates we're copying too much. Also add a slow-path trace for requests that triggered compaction.

sanjay: Implementation plan proposal: phase 1 (2 weeks): add PageView API + capability bits + metrics + unit tests; phase 2 (3 weeks): implement host-side stitch copy path + kernel opt-in; phase 3 (4 weeks): implement scatter-gather kernel and hot-pool; phase 4 (ongoing): compaction + heuristics.

megan: One more subtlety: GC/compaction must preserve KV slot ids used by models for cache coherence across sequences. If we move entries we must update any sequence-local pointers. That implies sequences must not hold raw device pointers across requests unless pinned. Use opaque `KVHandle` objects that invalidate on compaction.

alex: Yep. That's why `release_handle()` is critical. Also add `KVHandle.validate()` for debug builds.

build-bot: CI: `kv_pager_unit_tests` passed on branch `blockpager-interop` (build 4789) :white_check_mark:

maria: Ok next actions: alex to draft small PR for PageView API + metrics. sanjay to run cost microbench (copy vs scatter) on A100/RTX; megan to draft compaction safety doc. I'll follow up with concrete alert thresholds.

alex: I'll open the PR today and tag y'all. Thanks — want to avoid redoing kernels mid-release window. :thumbsup:
